newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AIM FOR REVENGE AGAINST GERMANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AIM FOR REVENGE AGAINST GERMANS.

text.p: Atletico Madrid coach Radomir Antic will be hoping to rewrite one of the most painful pages in the club's history when his side meet Borussia Dortmund in Wednesday's Champions' League clash in the European Cup.
Atletico came within a whisker of winning the final of the European Cup in 1974, the last time they met a German side in the premier continental competition.
But Bayern Munich scored a last-gasp equaliser and Franz Beckenbauer's side went on to win the replay 4-0.
It was a heavy blow for Atletico, who at times have struggled to escape the shadow of neighbours Real, winners of a record six European Cups.
Antic, himself a former Real coach, lifted Atletico to their first-ever domestic league and cup double last season.
Few Spaniards would be surprised to see the Serbian take his team all the way to the final after a fine Champions' League debut in Group B.
Atletico have the best record of any side in the competition after beating former champions Steaua Bucharest 4-0 and winning 4-1 at Poland's Widzew Lodz.
But Borussia Dortmund have also beaten both Steaua and Widzew and will provide the toughest opposition in the group for Atletico.

Injury deprives Dortmund of influential sweeper Matthias Sammer, midfielder Andreas Moeller and defender Rene Schneider, all Germany internationals. But Brazilian defender Julio Cesar is getting over a muscle injury and is likely to play.
Dortmund beat Duisburg 2-0 German in the German league last Saturday but they are not performing well in midfield or attack.

"We're not going to Madrid as favourites but we don't want to lose there either," trainer Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "We have to live with lots of injuries but it gives the replacements a chance to force their way in."
Dortmund may draw strength from the past, having beaten Atletico in the quarter-finals of the European Cup Winners' Cup on their way to winning the trophy in the 1965/66 season.
Atletico's superb European form has contrasted with some very ordinary performances at home and the Madrid club are already six points adrift of leaders Barcelona after seven league games.
One of the reasons behind Atletico's poor run has been a series of injuries to international playmaker Jose Luis Caminero, who will miss the Borussia match with a muscle strain.
To make matters worse even Antic himself is injured.
The Serbian pulled up in training on Sunday after aggravating an old Achilles tendon injury from his time as a player and will have to curb his animated touchline sorties.

But Antic will be cheered by the reappearance of international striker Kiko Narvaez, who sat out Saturday's 2-2 draw with Real Betis. "It's an important game, which could open the way to the quarter-finals," Kiko said.

Midfielder Diego Simeone said the game would not be easy "The Germans are the players I respect most in the world," said Simeone, who has surprisingly usurped the role of goalscorer from another Argentine, target-man Juan Eduardo Esnaider.
Simeone's brave headed goals, particularly at set-pieces from Serbian specialist Milinko Pantic, have made him leading scorer in the Champions' League.
The match should fill Atletico's Vicente Calderon stadium for the first time this season. The capacity has been reduced by 6,000 to just under 50,000 because of engineering works.
Probable teams:
Atletico Madrid - Jose Molina; Santi Denia, Roberto Solozabal, Toni Munoz, Delfi Geli; Juan Solozabal, Radek Bejbl, Diego Simeone, Milinko Pantic; Kiko Narvaez, Juan Eduardo Esnaider
Borussia Dortmund - Stefan Klos; Wolfgang Feiersinger, Juergen Kohler, Julio Cesar, Stefan Reuter; Paul Lambert, Michael Zorc, Rene Tretschok, Joerg Heinrich; Lars Ricken, Stephane Chapuisat.
